description: Discover how bioprocesses are mathematically modeled, optimized, and controlled using Quality by Design (QbD) principles.

slides.title: Welcome to Process Optimization
slides.content:
# Process Optimization

Welcome to Process Optimization!

Once a process works, how do we make it better, faster, and more reliable?

## What You Will Learn:
- **Process Modeling**: Using math to predict biology.
- **Parameter Optimization**: Finding the "sweet spot" (DoE).
- **Quality by Design (QbD)**: Designing quality in from the start.
- **Process Analytical Technology (PAT)**: Real-time monitoring.

slides.title: Process Modeling
slides.content:
# Process Modeling

A **Model** is a mathematical representation of a biological or physical process.

## Types of Models:
1. **Mechanistic Models (White Box)**: Based on actual physical/biological laws (e.g., Monod kinetics for cell growth based on substrate consumption). Highly accurate but very hard to build.
2. **Empirical Models (Black Box)**: Based purely on data statistics (e.g., Artificial Neural Networks). The model finds patterns linking inputs to outputs without "understanding" the biology.
3. **Hybrid Models**: Combine both approaches.

slides.title: Why Use Models?
slides.content:
# The Power of Modeling

Why spend months doing math?

- **Prediction**: Predict how much drug will be produced in 14 days without actually running a 14-day experiment.
- **Optimization**: Find the theoretically perfect feeding strategy before touching a bioreactor.
- **Troubleshooting**: If a batch fails, a model can help identify which parameter (e.g., a temperature spike on day 3) was responsible.

> **Digital Twins**: The ultimate goal is a "Digital Twin" - a real-time virtual replica of the physical bioreactor.

slides.title: Modeling Quiz
slides.quizQuestion: Which type of process model relies purely on statistical patterns in data rather than underlying physical or biological laws?

slides.title: Parameter Optimization
slides.content:
# Parameter Optimization

A bioprocess has dozens of variables (pH, Temp, Dissolved Oxygen, feed rate, agitation). How do you find the best combination?

## The Old Way: OFAT
**One-Factor-At-a-Time (OFAT)**:
- Keep everything constant, change Temperature. Find the best Temp.
- Keep new Temp constant, change pH. Find the best pH.
- **Problem**: This completely misses *interactions* between variables (e.g., maybe high Temp is only good if pH is also high). It's also very slow.

slides.title: Design of Experiments (DoE)
slides.content:
# Design of Experiments (DoE)

**DoE** is a statistical approach to optimization.

## How DoE Works:
- Instead of changing one thing at a time, you change *multiple* variables simultaneously in a highly structured matrix of experiments.
- A software program analyzes the results and generates a 3D surface map of the process.
- It mathematically identifies both the main effects AND the interactions between variables.

> **Result**: DoE finds the true, global optimal conditions with far fewer experiments than OFAT.

slides.title: DoE Quiz
slides.quizQuestion: What is a major advantage of using Design of Experiments (DoE) over the One-Factor-At-a-Time (OFAT) approach?
quizOptions: DoE requires only a single experiment
DoE ignores the effects of pH and temperature
DoE can identify complex interactions between multiple variables
DoE does not require any mathematical analysis

slides.title: Quality by Design (QbD)
slides.content:
# Quality by Design (QbD)

**QbD** is a modern regulatory framework championed by the FDA.

## Traditional Approach:
"Test into compliance." Make a batch, test it at the end. If it fails, throw it away. (High waste, poor understanding).

## QbD Approach:
"Quality is built into the product and process by design."
- You must thoroughly understand *why* the process works.
- You identify every parameter that could affect quality and prove you can control it.

slides.title: CQAs and CPPs
slides.content:
# The Vocabulary of QbD

## Critical Quality Attributes (CQAs)
Physical, chemical, or biological properties of the *drug itself* that must be within an appropriate limit to ensure desired product quality (e.g., Glycosylation pattern, protein aggregation %).

## Critical Process Parameters (CPPs)
Variables in the *manufacturing process* that impact a CQA and therefore should be monitored or controlled (e.g., Bioreactor pH, Chromatography flow rate).

> **The Goal**: By tightly controlling the CPPs, you guarantee the CQAs will be met, every single time.

slides.title: The Design Space
slides.content:
# The Design Space

By executing DoE studies, engineers define the **Design Space**.

## Definition:
The multidimensional combination and interaction of input variables (CPPs) that have been demonstrated to provide assurance of quality.

## Regulatory Benefit:
If you file a Design Space with the FDA, you are legally allowed to change your process parameters *anywhere within that space* without having to ask the FDA for permission again. This offers massive manufacturing flexibility.

slides.title: Process Analytical Technology (PAT)
slides.content:
# Process Analytical Technology (PAT)

If QbD is the philosophy, **PAT** is the tool that makes it happen.

## What is PAT?
PAT is a system for designing, analyzing, and controlling manufacturing through **timely measurements** (i.e., during processing) of critical quality and performance attributes.

## Traditional vs PAT:
- **Traditional**: Take a sample, send to lab, wait 2 days for results.
- **PAT**: A probe inside the bioreactor measures the attribute in real-time, allowing the control system to instantly correct any deviations.

slides.title: Examples of PAT Tools
slides.content:
# PAT in Action

What kind of sensors do we use?

- **Raman Spectroscopy**: A laser probe inside the tank that reads the molecular "fingerprint" of the broth. It can measure glucose, lactate, and even cell density simultaneously in real-time.
- **Dielectric Spectroscopy (Capacitance)**: Measures the electrical capacitance of the broth, which directly correlates to the *viable* (living) cell mass, ignoring dead cells.
- **At-line HPLC**: Automated systems that pull a tiny sample every hour and run a fast chromatography assay right next to the bioreactor.

slides.title: PAT Quiz
slides.content: Test your knowledge on real-time analysis.
slides.quizQuestion: What is the primary goal of Process Analytical Technology (PAT)?
quizOptions: To reduce the number of operators needed
To perform real-time measurements during the process to enable immediate control and correction
To test the final product after manufacturing is complete
To design the physical layout of the facility

slides.title: Module Summary
slides.content:
# Process Optimization Summary

## Key Takeaways:
- **Modeling**: Uses math (Mechanistic or Empirical) to predict and troubleshoot bioprocesses.
- **DoE**: A statistical method to optimize multiple parameters simultaneously, finding interactions that OFAT misses.
- **QbD**: A regulatory framework focused on building quality into the process by understanding how CPPs affect CQAs.
- **Design Space**: The safe operating range proven to yield good product.
- **PAT**: Real-time sensors (like Raman) used to measure and control the process live.

> **Congratulations!** You have completed the Process Optimization module.
